newsitem.title: POLAND: White House has no comment on Bosnian police raid.
newsitem.headline: White House has no comment on Bosnian police raid.

text.p: A spokesman for U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Thursday the White House had no immediate comment on a clash between NATO-led peacekeeping troops and a hardline Bosnian Serb police chief.
"I don't have anything for you on that," spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
Clinton arrived in Poland on Thursday from Spain where a NATO summit in Madrid invited Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to talks on joining the Western alliance.
Britain confirmed that hardline Bosnian Serb police chief Simo Drljaca was killed in a clash with NATO-led peacekeeping troops on Thursday.

Berger said the operation was in a sector of Bosnia policed by British peacekeeping troops and that Simo Drljaca, the former police chief of the northwest town of Prijedor, was shot dead in self-defence during it.

He said another war crimes suspect, Milan Kovacevic, director of a Prijador hospital, was detained without incident and would be turned over to the international war crimes tribunal in The Hague for trial.

The U.S. national security adviser refused to publicly discuss other details of the incident. But a White House official who asked not to be identified said Clinton had been briefed on planning for the operation late last week and gave his approval.

"We do not expect any reaction, but if there was one, SFOR would react firmly to any reaction," the official said. He said Drljaca and Kovacevic were targeted because they were "coming into very frequent contact" with SFOR troops, but added that no one suspected of war crimes in Bosnia was considered immune from arrest.
